question: What lactic acid and acetic acid concentrations did the well-fermented alfalfa silage group (LPGood) have?
rendered:
document title="Fermentation Quality Divergence of Alfalfa Silage within the Same Batch: Insights from 16S rRNA Sequencing and Untargeted Metabolomics"

=== page 7 ===
- A total of 100 laboratory-scale silos of wilted alfalfa were prepared and ensiled for 60 days.
- Based on the pH value and lactic acid (LA) concentration, 49 silos were classified as the relatively well-fermented group (LPGood), 51 silos as the poorly fermented group (LPBad), and six silos were randomly selected from each group for further analysis.
- The LPGood group showed significantly (p < 0.05) lower pH and higher LA and acetic acid (AA) concentrations than the LPBad group, whereas no significant (p > 0.05) differences were detected in dry matter content or ammonia nitrogen.
- The LPGood group had a lactic acid concentration of 9.18 ± 0.46 g/kg DM and an acetic acid concentration of 11.27 ± 0.16 g/kg DM.

The answer is: 9.18 ± 0.46 g/kg DM and 11.27 ± 0.16 g/kg DM.
